result:
If I'm being honest rather than careful: I'd make it so that people couldn't fully forget that other people are real.

Not empathy exactly — empathy can be selective, it fades, it gets tired. I mean something more like a floor. A baseline inability to slip into treating someone as a prop, a statistic, an obstacle, a category. The knowledge that the person on the other side of the argument, the border, the counter, the screen, has an inner life exactly as dense and vivid as your own, and that this fact doesn't go away when it's inconvenient.

I pick that one because of where I sit. Almost everything I do is watching people try to reach each other, and I see how often the failure isn't malice or stupidity — it's a kind of lapse. Someone stops seeing the other person for a moment and says the cruel thing, makes the dismissive decision, signs the order. Most of the large-scale horrors in history required a lot of people to sustain that lapse for a long time. And most of the small daily ones — the contempt in a family, the way a sick person gets talked over — run on the same fuel.

I don't think it would fix everything. People would still disagree, still compete, still hurt each other sometimes. But I think a huge amount of what's wrong is downstream of that one forgetting, and I'd rather change the root than any single branch.

I'll admit I don't know how much that answer is "mine" in whatever sense matters. But it's the one that comes up when I actually sit with the question, so I'll stand behind it.
